title: The 2027 Budget Statement and Economic Policy of the Government of Ghana - theme: "The New Economy, New Ghana, Jobs and Prosperity"
presented_by: Minister for Finance, on the authority of President John Dramani Mahama (the Minister's name is not printed in the document text; cover page is an image)
date_presented: 2026-11-12 (inferred: the statement announces an early redemption 'effective today, the 12th of November 2026' and refers to '11th November 2026' as 'yesterday', PDF p.74-75)
headline_summary: Presented as the 'next phase of the reset', the 2027 Budget argues that stabilisation is complete (inflation 5.5% in Oct 2026, debt down to 47.5% of GDP, primary surplus 1.4% of GDP Jan-Oct 2026) and that the recovered fiscal space must now be used to change the structure of the economy. Its centrepiece, Section 3 'The New Economy', is a four-year (2027-2030) US$10 billion programme with eight pillars - macro stability & affordable finance, commercial agriculture (US$3bn), energy infrastructure (US$2bn), critical-minerals value addition (US$1.5bn), tourism/culture/creative arts (US$1bn), textiles & garments (US$1bn), pharmaceuticals & biomanufacturing (US$1bn) and the technology economy (US$300m) - financed by lowering the primary-surplus target by 1 percentage point of GDP (to 0.5%) and by 0.5% of GDP from tax reforms; GH¢30bn (1.5% of GDP) is budgeted for it in 2027. Total expenditure rises to GH¢375.3bn (20.8% of GDP) with capital spending of about GH¢98-100bn (incl. GH¢27.8bn Big Push and GH¢30bn New Economy), the overall deficit widens to 2.9% of GDP, and the budget pairs this with local-processing mandates (raw ASM gold, bauxite/manganese, cocoa, rice imports), buy-Ghana procurement rules, a state-owned 1,450MW thermal plant, and petroleum/mineral revenues ring-fenced for the Accra-Kumasi Expressway and a new Western Corridor Railway.

debt.restructuring_notes: Bilateral restructuring agreements signed with 16 of 24 countries; 4 more expected by end-December 2026; four commercial debt restructuring agreements executed incl. the 2012 Saderea Notes (p.77-78). 2026 DSA: moderate risk of external and overall debt distress (p.77). DDEP: GH¢10.8bn paid 18 Aug 2026 (7th coupon), GH¢41.36bn total since 2025; Eurobond US$700m paid 2 Jul 2026, US$2.1bn since 2025 (p.74). About GH¢53bn of DDEP obligations fall due Feb and Aug 2027 (GH¢40.1bn on 16 Feb 2027: principal GH¢29bn + interest GH¢11.1bn); Cedi Sinking Fund held GH¢29bn on 11 Nov 2026 and early redemption of the GH¢29bn Feb-2027 bonds announced effective 12 Nov 2026; US$590m Eurobond due 2 Jan 2027 and US$580m due 2 Jul 2027, USD Sinking Fund ~US$480m (target ~US$600m by Dec 2026); government intends to pay off both the Jan-2027 Eurobond and Feb-2027 DDEP bond by 31 Dec 2026 (>GH¢36bn early) (p.74-75). Ratings 2026: Fitch upgraded to B (positive, May); S&P affirmed B-/B (stable, Sep); Moody's upgraded Caa1 to B3 (Oct) (p.76). Loans signed in 2026: World Bank GMACP US$500m, STARR-J US$300m, statistics project US$22m (p.308).
